description:
I'm looking for teammates who are creative, motivated, reliable, and willing to contribute actively throughout the hackathon. Skills in data analysis, scientific research, UI/UX design, web development, or experience working with NASA datasets would be especially valuable.

You don't need to be an expert. What matters most is curiosity, teamwork, commitment, and the willingness to turn an idea into something meaningful. Let's build something worth remembering!
summary: VIIRSMode harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into one continuous series and turns it into a burning-activity calendar for any selected area, with historical-median comparison and CSV export.
details:
PROBLEM

MODIS has observed fires since 2000, but VIIRS sees smaller fires at finer resolution, so their records cannot be compared directly. Adding VIIRS makes fire activity look higher only because a better sensor arrived. MODIS is also approaching the end of its life, so any long fire history needs a way to continue with VIIRS.

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

VIIRSMode harmonizes NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections in two steps.

1) Grouping: detections from the same UTC day within 1 km and with similar fire radiative power (FRP) are grouped, so one fire seen by several satellites counts once. We keep only detections classified as presumed vegetation fire (FIRMS type 0 or unclassified), which removes static land sources, volcanoes and offshore detections.

2) Weighting: for each period with the same set of VIIRS satellites (2000-2011 MODIS only; 2012-2017 MODIS + S-NPP; 2018 onward MODIS + S-NPP + NOAA-20), one constant weight scales the grouped counts to MODIS-equivalent units. The result is a consistent series from 2000 onward in which the sensor of origin no longer drives the trend.

THE WEB APPLICATION

A full-screen 3D globe shows the detections of the selected years. Users search a place by name or coordinates, or click any hotspot, and get:

- Hotspot details: date, sensor, satellite and fire radiative power.

- A burning-activity calendar (year by month) built from the harmonized series, with an accessible, color-blind-friendly color ramp.

- A comparison of any month against the historical median of the same calendar month for that area.

- A CSV download of the detections for the selected area and years, including the harmonization weights.

- Go Live: Live shows the last 24 h of NOAA-20 VIIRS detections through a serverless proxy that keeps the FIRMS key private; low-confidence detections are filtered and up to 15,000 points are shown.

- A "Why" section explaining fire regimes and why MODIS and VIIRS must be harmonized.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Emergency responders, early-warning teams, scientists and land managers get one consistent fire history instead of two records that cannot be compared. They can see which months and years had the most activity, whether the current month is above or below normal for an area, and download the data for their own analysis. Because the weighting is defined per period of satellite coverage, the approach can be extended as satellites change (for example NOAA-21, or the end of S-NPP deliveries on November 2, 2026).

HOW WE VALIDATED IT

In our Portugal data (2000-2025), the harmonized yearly counts differ from MODIS by about 12.2% on average across the years with VIIRS. This is an approximation, not a sensor calibration. Limits: the demo data covers Portugal only, with S-NPP and NOAA-20 (no NOAA-21 and no 2026 data yet); the weights assume a stable ratio within each period; and they are validated on the same years used to compute them. Years with little fire activity show larger relative errors. The grouping parameters (radius, FRP tolerance) are adjustable and every run writes a report with counts before and after harmonization.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Data: NASA FIRMS archive (MODIS Collection 6.1, VIIRS 375 m S-NPP and NOAA-20). Importer and harmonization: Python (standard library only) with automated tests. Web app: JavaScript, Vue 3, Vite and CesiumJS, with Esri World Imagery as basemap and OpenStreetMap Nominatim for place search. The project is built on top of the open-source gods-eye-view project (MIT license), from which we reused the scaffolding and dependencies; the ViirsMode page, the globe view, the harmonization importer and the data are new work done during the hackathon. We used AI assistants (Claude and GitHub Copilot) to help write and debug code; the method, parameters and validation were run and reviewed by the team.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

Instead of simply merging two datasets, we treat the sensor change itself as the problem: grouping removes double counting of the same fire, and per-period weights turn a patchwork of sensors into one continuous, comparable calendar, shown on an interactive globe.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Different pixel sizes, observation times and sensitivities of MODIS and VIIRS; duplicate and non-vegetation detections; the changing set of satellites over time; accessible color choices; transparency about what the numbers mean (counts are daily hotspot groups in MODIS-equivalent units, not individual fires); and keeping all the steps reproducible.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Earthdata): MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS 375 m (S-NPP, NOAA-20) active-fire archives for Portugal, 2000-2025.
